query: Let `T : E →L[𝕜] E` be a compact self-adjoint operator on a complete inner product space `E`. Then the orthogonal complement of `⨆ μ, eigenspace T μ` (the closed span of all eigenspaces) is `⊥`, i.e. the eigenspaces of `T` together span a dense subspace of `E`.

    18  
    19  This file covers the spectral theory of self-adjoint operators on an inner product space.
    20  
    21  The first part of the file covers general properties, true without any condition on boundedness or
    22  compactness of the operator or finite-dimensionality of the underlying space, notably:

    24  * `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces`: the eigenspaces are orthogonal

    27  
    28  The second part of the file covers properties of self-adjoint operators in finite dimension.
    29  Letting `T` be a self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional inner product space `T`,
    30  * The definition `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.diagonalization` provides a linear isometry equivalence `E`
    31    to the direct sum of the eigenspaces of `T`.  The theorem
    32    `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.diagonalization_apply_self_apply` states that, when `T` is transferred via
    33    this equivalence to an operator on the direct sum, it acts diagonally.
    34  * The definition `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvectorBasis` provides an orthonormal basis for `E`
    35    consisting of eigenvectors of `T`, with `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` giving the
    36    corresponding list of eigenvalues, as real numbers.  The definition
    37    `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvectorBasis` gives the associated linear isometry equivalence
    38    from `E` to Euclidean space, and the theorem
    39    `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvectorBasis_apply_self_apply` states that, when `T` is
    40    transferred via this equivalence to an operator on Euclidean space, it acts diagonally.
    41  * `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` gives the eigenvalues in decreasing order.  This is
    42    done for several reasons: (i) This agrees with the standard convention of listing singular
    43    values in decreasing order, with the operator norm as the first singular value
    44    (ii) For positive compact operators on an infinite-dimensional space, one can list the nonzero
    45    eigenvalues in decreasing (but not increasing) order since they converge to zero. (iii) This
    46    simplifies several theorem statements. For example the Schur-Horn theorem states that the diagonal
